correctness.rationale: For the explicitly normalized type-C upper Gale interval, feasible binary vertices are precisely reversed length-2r simple walks constrained to height >= -1; reflection gives binom(2r+1,r) vertices. A complementary feasible pair has both height h and -h >= -1, so each even time has height zero and yields 2^(r-1) unordered diameter pairs. A pair at squared distance 2r-1 has exactly one equal bit, necessarily zero. Decomposing at its position leaves a five-state walk on -1,0,1,2,3; the two-step continuation recurrence has row sum three, giving 3^m and 2*3^m. Both parity sums have 2(3^r-2^r) ordered pairs, hence exactly 2(3^r-2^r) unordered near-diameter pairs in total. Strict convexity excludes nonvertex diametral endpoints. Verified independently by complete integer vertex-pair enumeration for r=1..6 (1,586,479 pairs) and a separate integer dynamic program for r=1..15, run from this package.

value.rationale: The two maximal Euclidean chord shells and the complete diameter graph are canonical metric invariants of a natural infinite family of non-snake type-C feasible polytopes. The exponential ratio 4((3/2)^r-1) separates top and almost-top distances and the proof supplies a compact two-walk/five-state defect method. The result is exact for all dimensions and does not rely on arbitrary parameter slicing or a finite table.
